nodes.description: Private uint256 holding the secret number (1-16) regenerated by shuffle() after every play().
Public uint256 recording the timestamp of the last play() call; used in the kill() time gate.
Public uint256 bet price (0.2 ether) that msg.value must meet in play().
Public address of the owner, set from msg.sender in the constructor and used to authorize kill().
Public array of Game structs recording every player and guessed number.
Constructor: assigns ownerAddr = msg.sender and calls shuffle() to initialize the secret.
Internal function that derives secretNumber from sha3(now, block.blockhash(block.number-1)) % 16 + 1 (predictable randomness).
Payable public game loop: validates bet, stores the Game, pays the whole balance on a correct guess, then re-shuffles and sets lastPlayed.
Owner-only, time-gated function that destroys the contract and sends its balance to msg.sender via suicide().
Payable fallback function, invoked on plain ether transfers and reachable by a re-entrant call during payout.
Caller-controlled address used for ownership, player identity, and payout destinations.
now / block.timestamp, used as randomness seed, as stored lastPlayed, and in the kill() time check.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) in play(): external call forwarding the entire contract balance to an untrusted address.
suicide(msg.sender) in kill(): selfdestruct-style primitive that force-sends the balance and terminates the contract.
sha3(now, block.blockhash(block.number-1)) used to derive secretNumber; miner-controllable and predictable randomness.
now > lastPlayed + 6 hours timestamp arithmetic governing the kill() authorization window.
Caller-supplied guessed number for play(), required to be <= 16 and compared against secretNumber.
Local Game struct instance in play() that is populated with msg.sender and number and pushed to gamesPlayed.

edges.reason: Constructor stores msg.sender into ownerAddr, establishing the privileged account from an untrusted caller address.
msg.sender is written into game.player and later reused as the payout recipient inside play().
suicide(msg.sender) forwards the remaining balance to the address derived from msg.sender.
block.timestamp seeds the shuffle() randomness, making secretNumber predictable from timestamp/blockhash.
play() assigns now to lastPlayed, a timestamp dependency that later governs kill().
kill() compares now against a stored time, so its authorization depends on block.timestamp.
secretNumber is compared with the player's guess to decide the payout branch.
shuffle() is the writer of secretNumber, refreshing it after every attempt.
betPrice bounds msg.value in the play() require statement.
lastPlayed participates in the time gate condition of kill().
ownerAddr is compared with msg.sender to authorize the destructive kill() call.
The weak sha3/timestamp/blockhash hash feeds directly into the stored secretNumber.
The lastPlayed + 6 hours arithmetic is evaluated in kill()'s authorization condition.
The constructor unconditionally invokes shuffle() to initialize the game state.
play() calls shuffle() after each guess to pick a new secret number.
On a winning guess play() executes the external balance transfer to the untrusted player before finishing state updates.
play() pushes the constructed Game record into the gamesPlayed array.
play() writes now into lastPlayed, creating the timestamp dependency consumed by kill().
kill() reaches suicide(msg.sender) only through the owner and timestamp checks, so the destructive call is access-controlled.
The external transfer to msg.sender can invoke the contract's payable fallback, re-entering the contract mid-payout.

normalization_plan.reason: The number parameter exists only as the caller's guess consumed by play()'s validation and win comparison, so it should be folded into the play node.
The local Game struct is a temporary record created, filled with msg.sender/number, and pushed to gamesPlayed entirely inside play(), so it should be folded into the play node.
